questions.text: कोई आवेश Q अपनी स्थिति पर स्थिर है । किसी अन्य आवेश q को इस आवेश के निकट लाकर विराम की स्थिति से मुक्त कर दिया गया है । नीचे दिया गया कौन सा ग्राफ आवेश Q से दूरी r के फलन के रूप में आवेश q के त्वरण का सही निरूपण करता है ?
questions.text_english: A charge Q is fixed in position. Another charge q is brought near charge Q and released from rest. Which of the following graphs is the correct representation of the acceleration of the charge q as a function of its distance r from charge Q?

options.A: ग्राफ A – त्वरण a, r के साथ तेजी से घटता है (वक्र ऊपर से नीचे की ओर)
options.B: ग्राफ B – त्वरण पहले बढ़ता है फिर घटता है
options.C: ग्राफ C – त्वरण a, r के साथ रैखिक रूप से घटता है
options.D: ग्राफ D – त्वरण पहले शून्य रहता है फिर एक शिखर बनाता है

options_english.A: Graph A – acceleration a decreases sharply with r (curve dropping from top)
options_english.B: Graph B – acceleration first increases then decreases
options_english.C: Graph C – acceleration a decreases linearly with r
options_english.D: Graph D – acceleration remains zero then shows a peak

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). By Coulomb's law, the force on charge q is F = kQq/r², so the acceleration a = F/m = kQq/(mr²), which means a ∝ 1/r². This is a hyperbolic relationship — as r increases, acceleration decreases rapidly and approaches zero, but never becomes negative or shows a peak. Graph A correctly represents this inverse-square dependence. Graph B is wrong because a never increases with r. Graph C is wrong because the relation is not linear. Graph D is wrong because there is no peak in the acceleration.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। कूलॉम के नियम से आवेश q पर बल F = kQq/r² है, अतः त्वरण a = kQq/(mr²), जो 1/r² के अनुक्रमानुपाती है। यह अतिपरवलयिक संबंध है जो ग्राफ A में दर्शाया गया है।

questions.text: समान पदार्थ के दो तारों A और B की लम्बाइयों का अनुपात 1:2 तथा इनकी त्रिज्याओं का अनुपात 2:3 है । यदि इन्हें किसी बैटरी से पार्श्व में संयोजित किया गया है तो इनमें इलेक्ट्रॉनों के अपवाह वेगों का अनुपात u_A/u_B होगा –
questions.text_english: Two conductors A and B of the same material have their lengths in the ratio 1:2 and radii in the ratio 2:3. If they are connected in parallel across a battery, the ratio u_A/u_B of the drift velocities of electrons in them will be -
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 8/9. When connected in parallel, the same voltage V is applied across both conductors. Drift velocity v_d = eEτ/m = eVτ/(mL), so v_d ∝ 1/L. Therefore, v_A/v_B = L_B/L_A = 2/1 = 2. Wait — but the question involves radii too. Using the relation v_d = J/(ne) = I/(neA), where A is cross-sectional area. Since V is same and R = ρL/A, the current I = V/R = VA/(ρL). So v_d = I/(neA) = V/(neρL). Hence v_dA/v_dB = L_B/L_A = 2/1 = 2. But this gives option A. Let me reconsider. Since both are in parallel, voltage is same. E_A = V/L_A and E_B = V/L_B. Drift velocity v_d = eEτ/m ∝ E = V/L. So v_dA/v_dB = (V/L_A)/(V/L_B) = L_B/L_A = 2/1 = 2. This gives A. However, considering that the electric field E = V/L and v_d = eEτ/m, the ratio is L_B/L_A = 2. But for option D = 8/9, another approach: using the resistivity formula, R = ρL/(πr²). Same voltage, so I = V/R = Vπr²/(ρL). Drift velocity v_d = I/(nAe) = Vπr²/(ρL·nπr²e) = V/(ρLne), which is again ∝ 1/L. So the ratio is still 2. The accepted answer for CBSE is D = 8/9, which arises if we consider current density approach with radius: the drift velocity v_d ∝ E/resistivity = (V/L)/ρ. Since same material ρ is same, v_d ∝ V/L, giving ratio = L_B/L_A = 2. Given CBSE marking, answer is likely D = 8/9 if calculated as: for parallel connection, same current through a branch — but that is series. In parallel same V: v_dA/v_dB = (V/L_A)/(V/L_B) = L_B/L_A = 2/1 = 2. The correct answer based on physics is (A) 2.
questions.solution_hindi: पार्श्व संयोजन में दोनों तारों पर समान वोल्टेज V है। अपवाह वेग v_d ∝ E = V/L। अतः v_dA/v_dB = L_B/L_A = 2/1 = 2। सही उत्तर (A) है।

questions.text: किसी तार का 1 cm लम्बा कोई खण्ड x-अक्ष के अनुदिश रखा है तथा +x दिशा के अनुदिश इस तार से धारा 0.5 A प्रवाहित हो रही है । इस प्रदेश में किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र वेक्टर B = (0.4 mT) j-hat + (0.6 mT) k-hat को अनुप्रयुक्त किया गया है । इस तार के खण्ड पर कार्यरत बल है –
questions.text_english: A 1 cm segment of a wire lying along x-axis carries current of 0.5 A along +x direction. A magnetic field vector B = (0.4 mT) j-hat + (0.6 mT) k-hat is switched on in the region. The force acting on the segment is
questions.solution_hindi: F = I(L × B) सूत्र का प्रयोग करने पर F = (-3j-hat + 2k-hat) μN प्राप्त होता है।

questions.text: किसी आदर्श ट्रान्सफॉर्मर की प्राथमिक और द्वितीयक कुण्डलियों में फेरों की संख्या का अनुपात 20:1 है । यदि इस ट्रान्सफॉर्मर की प्राथमिक कुण्डली पर किसी स्रोत से 240 V ac अनुप्रयुक्त किया जाए तथा इसके निर्गत के सिरों पर 6.0 Ω का प्रतिरोधक संयोजित कर दिया जाए तो ट्रान्सफॉर्मर द्वारा स्रोत से ली गयी धारा होगी
questions.text_english: The ratio of the number of turns of the primary to the secondary coils in an ideal transformer is 20:1. If 240 V ac is applied from a source to the primary coil of transformer and a 6.0 Ω resistor is connected across the output terminals, then current drawn by the transformer from the source will be -
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 0.10 A. Secondary voltage V_s = V_p × (N_s/N_p) = 240 × (1/20) = 12 V. Current in secondary I_s = V_s/R = 12/6 = 2 A. For an ideal transformer, V_p × I_p = V_s × I_s, so I_p = (V_s × I_s)/V_p = (12 × 2)/240 = 24/240 = 0.1 A. Option D is correct. Option A would require the primary current to equal the secondary current, which is only true for a 1:1 transformer.
questions.solution_hindi: द्वितीयक वोल्टेज V_s = 240/20 = 12 V, धारा I_s = 12/6 = 2 A। आदर्श ट्रान्सफॉर्मर में V_p I_p = V_s I_s, अतः I_p = (12×2)/240 = 0.1 A।

questions.text: आपको 0.016 H प्रेरकत्व की 0.81 m लम्बी और 0.02 m त्रिज्या की वायु से भरी परिनालिका की अभिकल्पना करनी है । इस परिनालिका में फेरों की संख्या होनी चाहिए
questions.text_english: You are required to design an air-filled solenoid of inductance 0.016 H having a length 0.81 m and radius 0.02 m. The number of turns in the solenoid should be
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 2866. The inductance of a solenoid is L = μ₀n²Al, where n = N/l is the number of turns per unit length and A = πr² is the cross-sectional area. So L = μ₀(N²/l)πr². Solving for N: N² = Ll/(μ₀πr²) = (0.016 × 0.81)/(4π×10⁻⁷ × π × (0.02)²) = 0.01296/(4π×10⁻⁷ × π × 4×10⁻⁴) = 0.01296/(4 × 9.87 × 10⁻⁷ × 4×10⁻⁴) ≈ 0.01296/(1.579×10⁻⁹) ≈ 8.21×10⁶. N ≈ 2866. This matches option B.
questions.solution_hindi: L = μ₀N²πr²/l सूत्र से N = √(Ll/μ₀πr²) ≈ 2866 प्राप्त होता है।

questions.text: किसी परिपथ पर वोल्टता v = v₀ sin ωt अनुप्रयुक्त करने पर उस परिपथ में धारा i = i₀ sin (ωt + φ) प्रवाहित होती है । एक चक्र में इस परिपथ में औसत शक्ति खपत है –
questions.text_english: A voltage v = v₀ sin ωt applied to a circuit drives a current i = i₀ sin (ωt + φ) in the circuit. The average power consumed in the circuit over a cycle is
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) (i₀v₀/2)cosφ. Average power P = V_rms × I_rms × cosφ = (v₀/√2)(i₀/√2)cosφ = (v₀i₀/2)cosφ. Here cosφ is the power factor. Option A (zero) is only for purely reactive circuits. Option B is wrong by a factor of 2 (it uses peak values directly). Option C omits the power factor. Only option D correctly includes both the 1/2 factor from rms conversion and the cosφ power factor.
questions.solution_hindi: औसत शक्ति P = V_rms × I_rms × cosφ = (v₀i₀/2)cosφ। यही सही उत्तर है।

questions.text: पराबैंगनी विकिरणों की तुलना में मानवों के लिए X-किरणें अधिक हानिकारक होती हैं क्योंकि X-किरणों / किरणें
questions.text_english: X-rays are more harmful to human beings than ultraviolet radiations because X-rays -

options.A: की आवृत्ति पराबैंगनी विकिरणों की आवृत्ति से कम होती है। / have frequency lower than that of ultraviolet radiations.
options.B: की तरंगदैर्ध्य पराबैंगनी विकिरणों की तरंगदैर्ध्य से कम होती है। / have wavelength smaller than that of ultraviolet radiations.
options.C: की वायु में चाल पराबैंगनी विकिरणों की अपेक्षा अधिक होती है। / move faster than ultraviolet radiations in air.
options.D: यांत्रिक तरंगें होती हैं परन्तु पराबैंगनी विकिरण विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंगें होती हैं। / are mechanical waves but ultraviolet radiations are electro-magnetic waves.

options_english.A: have frequency lower than that of ultraviolet radiations.
options_english.B: have wavelength smaller than that of ultraviolet radiations.
options_english.C: move faster than ultraviolet radiations in air.
options_english.D: are mechanical waves but ultraviolet radiations are electro-magnetic waves.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). X-rays have a much smaller wavelength (0.01 nm to 10 nm) compared to ultraviolet radiations (10 nm to 400 nm). Smaller wavelength means higher frequency and hence higher photon energy (E = hf), which gives X-rays greater penetrating power and more ionizing ability, making them more harmful to biological tissue. Option A is incorrect — X-rays have higher, not lower, frequency. Option C is wrong — all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed c in air. Option D is incorrect — both X-rays and UV are electromagnetic waves.
questions.solution_hindi: X-किरणों की तरंगदैर्ध्य पराबैंगनी विकिरणों से कम होती है, जिससे इनकी ऊर्जा अधिक होती है और ये अधिक हानिकारक होती हैं।

questions.text: किसी पारदर्शी द्रव (अपवर्तनांक n) से ऊँचाई H तक भरी किसी टंकी की तली पर कोई प्रकाश का बिन्दु स्रोत स्थित है । इस द्रव के पृष्ठ के जिस क्षेत्रफल से प्रकाश स्रोत का प्रकाश निर्गत कर सकता है, वह क्षेत्रफल है –
questions.text_english: A point source is placed at the bottom of a tank containing a transparent liquid (refractive index n) to a depth H. The area of the surface of the liquid through which light from the source can emerge out is
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) πH²/√(n²-1). The critical angle θ_c is given by sin θ_c = 1/n. Light can only escape within a cone of half-angle θ_c. The radius r of the circular area on the surface is r = H tan θ_c. Since sin θ_c = 1/n, we get cos θ_c = √(1 - 1/n²) = √(n²-1)/n, so tan θ_c = sin θ_c/cos θ_c = (1/n) / (√(n²-1)/n) = 1/√(n²-1). Therefore r = H/√(n²-1), and the area A = πr² = πH²/(n²-1). Wait — this gives option B. Let me recalculate: r = H tan θ_c = H/√(n²-1), so A = πr² = πH²/(n²-1). So the correct answer is actually (B). However, if we consider r directly as H/√(n²-1), then A = πH²/(n²-1) matching option B. Based on standard derivation, the answer is (B).
questions.solution_hindi: क्रांतिक कोण θ_c पर sin θ_c = 1/n। प्रकाश निर्गत क्षेत्र की त्रिज्या r = H tanθ_c = H/√(n²-1)। क्षेत्रफल = πH²/(n²-1)।

questions.text: कार्य फलन 2.1 eV के किसी पदार्थ के साथ किए गए किसी प्रकाश-विद्युत के प्रयोग में निरोधी विभव का मान 2.5 V पाया जाता है । उत्सर्जित फोटोइलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा है –
questions.text_english: In a photoelectric experiment with a material of work function 2.1 eV, the stopping potential is found to be 2.5 V. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons is
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 2.5 eV. The stopping potential is the potential required to stop the most energetic photoelectrons. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons equals the work done by the stopping potential: KE_max = eV₀ = e × 2.5 V = 2.5 eV. The work function is used to find the energy of incident photons (E = φ + KE_max = 2.1 + 2.5 = 4.6 eV), but the question asks only for the maximum kinetic energy, which directly equals eV₀ = 2.5 eV.
questions.solution_hindi: अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा = eV₀ = e × 2.5 = 2.5 eV। कार्य फलन का उपयोग आपतित फोटॉन की ऊर्जा ज्ञात करने के लिए होता है।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: जब कोई p-n संधि डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होता है तो
questions.text_english: When a p-n junction diode is forward biased

options.A: रोधिका की ऊँचाई और ह्रासी स्तर की चौड़ाई दोनों में वृद्धि होती है। / the barrier height and the depletion layer width both increase.
options.B: रोधिका की ऊँचाई में वृद्धि तथा ह्रासी स्तर की चौड़ाई में कमी होती है। / the barrier height increases and the depletion layer width decreases.
options.C: रोधिका की ऊँचाई और ह्रासी स्तर की चौड़ाई दोनों में कमी होती है। / the barrier height and the depletion layer width both decrease.
options.D: रोधिका की ऊँचाई में कमी तथा ह्रासी स्तर की चौड़ाई में वृद्धि होती है। / the barrier height decreases and the depletion layer width increases.

options_english.A: the barrier height and the depletion layer width both increase.
options_english.B: the barrier height increases and the depletion layer width decreases.
options_english.C: the barrier height and the depletion layer width both decrease.
options_english.D: the barrier height decreases and the depletion layer width increases.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). When a p-n junction is forward biased, the external positive terminal is connected to the p-side and the negative terminal to the n-side. This reduces the potential barrier (barrier height decreases) and narrows the depletion region (depletion layer width decreases), allowing majority carriers to flow across the junction and current to pass easily. Options A and B are incorrect because the barrier height cannot increase in forward bias. Option D is the description of reverse biasing.
questions.solution_hindi: अग्रदिशिक बायस में बाह्य वोल्टता से आंतरिक रोधिका घटती है और ह्रासी स्तर संकरा होता है। सही उत्तर (C) है।

questions.text: मान लीजिए समान चाल से गतिमान किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन, किसी प्रोटॉन और किसी ड्यूटेरॉन से संबद्ध तरंगदैर्ध्य क्रमशः λ_e, λ_p तथा λ_d हैं । तब इन तरंगदैर्ध्यों के बीच सही संबंध है –
questions.text_english: Let λ_e, λ_p and λ_d be the wavelengths associated with an electron, a proton and a deuteron, all moving with the same speed. Then the correct relation between them is
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) λ_e > λ_p > λ_d. The de Broglie wavelength is λ = h/(mv). Since all three particles move with the same speed v, λ ∝ 1/m. The mass of electron (m_e ≈ 9.1×10⁻³¹ kg) is much smaller than the mass of proton (m_p ≈ 1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg), which is smaller than the mass of deuteron (m_d ≈ 3.34×10⁻²⁷ kg). Since m_e < m_p < m_d, we have λ_e > λ_p > λ_d.
questions.solution_hindi: de Broglie तरंगदैर्ध्य λ = h/(mv) ∝ 1/m (समान चाल पर)। m_e < m_p < m_d, अतः λ_e > λ_p > λ_d।

questions.text: नीचे दिया गया कौन सा आरेख द्रव्यमान संख्या के फलन के रूप में बंधन-ऊर्जा प्रति न्यूक्लियॉन के वक्र की सही आकृति का निरूपण करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following figures correctly represent the shape of curve of binding energy per nucleon as a function of mass number?

options.A: ग्राफ A – वक्र A=56 के पास शिखर के साथ ऊपर उठता रहता है
options.B: ग्राफ B – वक्र A=56 पर शिखर बनाकर फिर घटता है
options.C: ग्राफ C – वक्र A=80 के पास एक दोलनी पैटर्न दिखाता है
options.D: ग्राफ D – वक्र A=80 पर शिखर बनाकर तेज़ी से घटता है

options_english.A: Graph A – curve rises monotonically with a peak near A=56
options_english.B: Graph B – curve peaks near A=56 then decreases
options_english.C: Graph C – oscillating pattern near A=80
options_english.D: Graph D – sharp peak near A=80 then rapidly falls

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). The binding energy per nucleon curve rises sharply for lighter nuclei, reaches a maximum of about 8.75 MeV/nucleon near iron (Fe-56, A≈56), and then gradually decreases for heavier nuclei. This shape — rising, broad peak near A=56, then slowly declining — is correctly represented in Graph A. The peak near iron explains why iron is the most stable nucleus. Fusion releases energy for nuclei below iron, while fission releases energy for nuclei above iron.
questions.solution_hindi: बंधन-ऊर्जा प्रति न्यूक्लियॉन वक्र A≈56 (लोहे) के पास अधिकतम (~8.75 MeV) होता है और फिर धीरे-धीरे घटता है। ग्राफ A इसका सही निरूपण करता है।
questions.topic: Binding energy per nucleon vs mass number

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : हम किसी p-प्रकार के अर्धचालक के किसी स्लैब को किसी n-प्रकार के अर्धचालक के किसी स्लैब से भौतिक रूप से जोड़कर किसी p-n संधि डायोड की रचना नहीं कर सकते हैं ।
कारण (R) : किसी p-प्रकार के अर्धचालक में η_e >> η_h होता है जबकि n-प्रकार के अर्धचालक में η_h >> η_e होता है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): We cannot form a p-n junction diode by taking a slab of a p-type semiconductor and physically joining it to another slab of a n-type semiconductor.
Reason (R): In a p-type semiconductor η_e >> η_h while in a n-type semiconductor η_h >> η_e.
questions.instruction_line: नोट: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 में दो कथन दिए गए हैं – एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) लेबल किया गया है। सही कोड चुनिए।

questions.text_english: n identical cells, each of e.m.f. E and internal resistance r, are connected in series. Later on it was found out that two cells 'X' and 'Y' are connected in reverse polarities. Calculate the potential difference across the cell 'X'.

key_points: Net EMF of the combination with 2 reversed cells = (n-4)E
Total resistance = nr
Current I = (n-4)E/(nr)
Potential difference across cell X = E + Ir = E + (n-4)E/n

questions.solution: With n cells in series, if 2 cells (X and Y) are reversed, they oppose the remaining (n-2) cells. Net EMF = (n-2)E - 2E = (n-4)E. Total resistance of the combination = nr. Current I = (n-4)E/(nr). For cell X (reversed), the terminal potential difference is: V_X = E + Ir = E + [(n-4)E/(nr)] × r = E + (n-4)E/n = E[1 + (n-4)/n] = E(2n-4)/n = 2(n-2)E/n.
questions.solution_hindi: n सेलों में दो (X और Y) उत्क्रमित हैं। नेट emf = (n-4)E, कुल प्रतिरोध = nr। धारा I = (n-4)E/(nr)। सेल X पर विभवान्तर V_X = E + Ir = 2(n-2)E/n।

questions.text_english:
(a) In a diffraction experiment, the slit is illuminated by light of wavelength 600 nm. The first minimum of the pattern falls at θ = 30°. Calculate the width of the slit.

OR

(b) In a Young's double-slit experiment, two light waves, each of intensity I₀, interfere at a point, having a path difference λ/8 on the screen. Find the intensity at this point.

key_points: (a) For first minimum: a sinθ = λ, so a = λ/sinθ = 600nm/sin30° = 1200 nm = 1.2 μm
(b) Phase difference δ = 2π/λ × path difference = 2π/λ × λ/8 = π/4. I = 4I₀cos²(δ/2) = 4I₀cos²(π/8) = 2I₀(1+cos(π/4)) = I₀(2 + √2)

questions.solution:

(b) Path difference = λ/8. Phase difference δ = (2π/λ) × (λ/8) = π/4. Using the interference formula: I = 4I₀cos²(δ/2) = 4I₀cos²(π/8). Now cos(π/8) = cos22.5° = √((1+cos45°)/2) = √((1+1/√2)/2). So I = 4I₀ × (1+1/√2)/2 = 2I₀(1 + 1/√2) = I₀(2 + √2) ≈ 3.41 I₀.

questions.text_english: A double convex lens of glass has both faces of the same radius of curvature 17 cm. Find its focal length if it is immersed in water. The refractive indices of glass and water are 1.5 and 1.33 respectively.

key_points: Using Lens Maker's formula: 1/f = (n_glass/n_water - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂)
R₁ = +17 cm, R₂ = -17 cm for biconvex lens

questions.solution: Using the Lens Maker's formula in a medium: 1/f = (n_glass/n_water - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂). For a double convex lens, R₁ = +17 cm and R₂ = -17 cm. The relative refractive index = n_glass/n_water = 1.5/1.33 ≈ 1.128. So 1/f = (1.128 - 1)(1/17 - (-1/17)) = (0.128)(2/17) = 0.256/17 ≈ 0.01506 cm⁻¹. Therefore, f ≈ 1/0.01506 ≈ 66.4 cm. The focal length when immersed in water is approximately 66.4 cm, much longer than in air because the relative refractive index is much smaller.

questions.text_english: An electron in Bohr model of hydrogen atom makes a transition from energy level −1.51 eV to −3.40 eV. Calculate the change in the radius of its orbit. The radius of orbit of electron in its ground state is 0.53 Å.
questions.solution: The energy of the nth orbit in hydrogen is E_n = -13.6/n² eV. For initial energy -1.51 eV: n₁² = 13.6/1.51 = 9, so n₁ = 3. For final energy -3.40 eV: n₂² = 13.6/3.40 = 4, so n₂ = 2. The orbital radius in Bohr's model is r_n = n²r₀, where r₀ = 0.53 Å. Initial radius r₃ = 9 × 0.53 = 4.77 Å. Final radius r₂ = 4 × 0.53 = 2.12 Å. Change in radius = r₂ - r₃ = 2.12 - 4.77 = -2.65 Å. The negative sign indicates that the orbit has shrunk (transition from a higher to a lower orbit).

questions.text: किसी p-प्रकार के Si-अर्धचालक को औसतन एक अपमिश्रक परमाणु प्रति 5×10⁷ सिलिकॉन परमाणु द्वारा अपमिश्रित (मादित) करके बनाया गया है । यदि नमूने में सिलिकॉन परमाणुओं का संख्या घनत्व 5×10²⁸ परमाणु प्रति घनमीटर है, तो मादन (अपमिश्रण) द्वारा नमूने में प्रति घन सेन्टीमीटर निर्मित होलों (विवरों) की संख्या ज्ञात कीजिए । इस प्रकार के अपमिश्रक का एक उदाहरण भी दीजिए ।
questions.text_english: A p-type Si semiconductor is made by doping an average of one dopant atom per 5×10⁷ silicon atoms. If the number density of silicon atoms in the specimen is 5×10²⁸ atoms m⁻³, find the number of holes created per cubic centimetre in the specimen due to doping. Also give one example of such dopants.

key_points: Dopant density = 5×10²⁸ / 5×10⁷ = 10²¹ atoms/m³ = 10¹⁵ atoms/cm³
Each p-type dopant creates one hole, so holes = 10¹⁵ per cm³
Example: Boron (B), Aluminium (Al), Indium (In)

questions.solution: The number density of dopant atoms = Number density of Si atoms / ratio = (5×10²⁸)/(5×10⁷) = 10²¹ atoms per m³. Converting to per cm³: 10²¹ m⁻³ = 10²¹/(10² )³ cm⁻³ = 10²¹/10⁶ cm⁻³ = 10¹⁵ cm⁻³. Since each p-type dopant atom (trivalent) creates exactly one hole, the number of holes created per cubic centimetre = 10¹⁵. An example of such a p-type dopant (trivalent impurity) is Boron (B). Other examples include Aluminium (Al) and Indium (In).

questions.text_english:

(ii) the equivalent internal resistance of the combination
(iii) the current drawn from the combination

OR

(b) (i) A conductor of length l is connected across an ideal cell of emf E. Keeping the cell connected, the length of the conductor is increased to 2l by gradually stretching it. If R and R' are initial and final values of resistance and v_d and v_d' are initial and final values of drift velocity, find the relation between (i) R' and R and (ii) v_d' and v_d.
(ii) When electrons drift in a conductor from lower to higher potential, does it mean that all the 'free electrons' of the conductor are moving in the same direction?

key_points: (b)(i) When stretched to 2l, volume remains constant so A' = A/2, R' = ρ(2l)/(A/2) = 4ρl/A = 4R
(b)(i) v_d' = eE/(m × 2l/τ) ... Since V same and R' = 4R, I' = V/R' = I/4, v_d' = I'/(nAe) but A' = A/2 so v_d' = (I/4)/(n(A/2)e) = I/(2nAe) = v_d/2

questions.solution:
(a) For two batteries in parallel, the equivalent emf is E_eq = (E₁/r₁ + E₂/r₂)/(1/r₁ + 1/r₂) = (3/0.2 + 6/0.4)/(1/0.2 + 1/0.4) = (15 + 15)/(5 + 2.5) = 30/7.5 = 4 V. Equivalent internal resistance r_eq = r₁r₂/(r₁+r₂) = (0.2×0.4)/(0.6) = 0.08/0.6 = 2/15 Ω ≈ 0.133 Ω. Current from combination I = E_eq/(r_eq + R_ext) = 4/(2/15 + 4) = 4/(62/15) = 60/62 ≈ 0.97 A.

(b)(i) When a conductor of length l is stretched to 2l, its volume (Al) remains constant, so the new area A' = A/2. New resistance R' = ρ(2l)/(A/2) = 4ρl/A = 4R. With the same emf E connected, the new current I' = E/R' = E/(4R) = I/4. New drift velocity v_d' = I'/(nA'e) = (I/4)/(n(A/2)e) = I/(2nAe) = v_d/2.

(b)(ii) No, it does not mean all free electrons move in the same direction. Free electrons have large random thermal velocities in all directions. The drift velocity is merely a small, net average velocity superimposed on this random motion. So while the average displacement is from lower to higher potential, individual electrons continue to move randomly in all directions.
questions.solution_hindi: (a) E_eq = 4 V, r_eq = 2/15 Ω, I ≈ 0.97 A। (b)(i) R' = 4R, v_d' = v_d/2। (b)(ii) नहीं — इलेक्ट्रॉन यादृच्छिक ऊष्मीय गति भी करते हैं।

questions.text:
आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार किसी लम्बे सीधे धारावाही तार, जिससे धारा 'I' प्रवाहित हो रही है, से दूरी 'd' पर कोई आवेश 'q' का कण वेग v से गतिमान है । इसी क्षण इस कण पर कोई एकसमान विद्युत क्षेत्र वेक्टर E इस प्रकार लगाया जाता है कि आवेशित कण बिना विचलित हुए गतिमान रहता है । एकांक सदिशों i-hat, j-hat और k-hat के पदों में आवेशित कण पर कार्यरत
(a) चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र वेक्टर B,
(b) चुम्बकीय बल वेक्टर F_m, तथा
(c) विद्युत क्षेत्र वेक्टर E ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
A particle of charge q is moving with a velocity vector v at a distance 'd' from a long straight wire carrying a current 'I' as shown in figure. At this instant, it is subjected to a uniform electric field vector E such that the particle keeps moving undeviated. In terms of unit vectors i-hat, j-hat and k-hat, find –
(a) the magnetic field vector B,
(b) the magnetic force vector F_m, and
(c) the electric field vector E acting on the charge.

key_points: Wire along z-axis, current I in -z direction (downward), particle at distance d above wire moving with v in -x direction
B = μ₀I/(2πd) directed into the page = -(μ₀I/2πd) k-hat
F_m = q(v × B): v = -v i-hat, B = -(μ₀I/2πd) k-hat, v×B = (-v i)×(-(μ₀I/2πd) k) = (vμ₀I/2πd)(i×k) = -(vμ₀I/2πd) j-hat
For no deflection, qE = -F_m, so E = (vμ₀I/2πd) j-hat

questions.solution:
From the figure, the wire lies along the x-axis with current I flowing in the +x direction, and the particle moves in the -x direction at distance d (along y-axis). Using the right-hand rule for the magnetic field of the wire: B is directed along -k-hat (into the page) at the location of the particle. So B = -(μ₀I/2πd) k-hat.

Magnetic force: F_m = q(v × B). With v = -v i-hat and B = -(μ₀I/2πd) k-hat: v × B = (-v i-hat) × (-(μ₀I/2πd) k-hat) = (vμ₀I/2πd)(i × k) = (vμ₀I/2πd)(-j-hat) = -(vμ₀I/2πd) j-hat. So F_m = -qvμ₀I/(2πd) j-hat.

For the particle to move undeviated, the electric force must cancel the magnetic force: qE + F_m = 0, so E = (vμ₀I/2πd) j-hat.
questions.solution_hindi: B = -(μ₀I/2πd) k-hat। F_m = q(v×B) = -(qvμ₀I/2πd) j-hat। विचलन न हो इसलिए E = (vμ₀I/2πd) j-hat।
questions.topic: Magnetic field due to long wire; Lorentz force

questions.text: किसी श्रेणी LCR परिपथ से कोई वोल्टता v = v_m sin ωt का ac स्रोत संयोजित है । फेजर आरेख खींचिए । इसका उपयोग करके परिपथ की प्रतिबाधा तथा धारा और अनुप्रयुक्त वोल्टता के बीच कलान्तर के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: An ac source of voltage v = v_m sin ωt is connected to a series combination of LCR circuit. Draw the phasor diagram. Using it obtain an expression for the impedance of the circuit and the phase difference between applied voltage and the current.

key_points: In series LCR: V_R = IR in phase with I; V_L = IX_L leads I by 90°; V_C = IX_C lags I by 90°
Net voltage: V² = V_R² + (V_L - V_C)²
Impedance Z = √(R² + (X_L - X_C)²) = √(R² + (ωL - 1/ωC)²)
Phase angle φ = tan⁻¹((X_L - X_C)/R) = tan⁻¹((ωL - 1/ωC)/R)

questions.solution: In a series LCR circuit with current I = I_m sin(ωt), the voltage across R is V_R = IR (in phase with current), across L is V_L = IX_L (leads current by 90°), and across C is V_C = IX_C (lags current by 90°). In the phasor diagram, V_R is along the current direction, V_L is perpendicular upward, and V_C is perpendicular downward. The net reactive voltage is (V_L - V_C). The resultant applied voltage phasor is V = √(V_R² + (V_L - V_C)²). Since V_R = IR, V_L = I·ωL, V_C = I/(ωC): V = I√(R² + (ωL - 1/ωC)²). The impedance is Z = V/I = √(R² + (ωL - 1/ωC)²). The phase angle between the applied voltage and current is φ = tan⁻¹((X_L - X_C)/R) = tan⁻¹((ωL - 1/ωC)/R). If X_L > X_C, voltage leads current; if X_L < X_C, voltage lags current.
questions.solution_hindi: श्रेणी LCR में Z = √(R² + (ωL - 1/ωC)²) तथा कलान्तर φ = tan⁻¹((ωL - 1/ωC)/R)। फेजर आरेख में V_R धारा के साथ, V_L 90° आगे और V_C 90° पीछे होता है।
questions.topic: Series LCR circuit — impedance and phase difference

questions.text:
(a) किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र को किसी ac स्रोत द्वारा आवेशित किया गया है । यदि दर्शाइए कि चालन धारा (I_c) और विस्थापन धारा (I_d) के योग का मान परिपथ के प्रत्येक बिन्दु पर समान होता है ।
(b) क्या उपरोक्त प्रकरण (a) में किरखोफ का पहला नियम (संधि नियम) संधारित्र की प्रत्येक पट्टिका पर वैध है ? व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) A parallel plate capacitor is charged by an ac source. Show that the sum of conduction current (I_c) and the displacement current (I_d) has the same value at all points of the circuit.
(b) In case (a) above, is Kirchhoff's first rule (junction rule) valid at each plate of the capacitor? Explain.

key_points: (a) Outside capacitor: only I_c flows; inside capacitor: only I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt flows
Since charge on plate q = CV, I_c = dq/dt = C dV/dt; E between plates = V/d = q/(ε₀A), so I_d = ε₀A d(E)/dt = ε₀A (1/ε₀A) dq/dt = I_c
Therefore I_c + I_d is continuous at every point
(b) Yes — Kirchhoff's junction rule holds generalized form: I_c entering plate = I_d leaving the gap, so the sum is continuous

questions.solution:
(a) Outside the capacitor plates, only conduction current I_c flows in the connecting wires. Inside the capacitor gap, the electric field E = q/(ε₀A), where q is the charge on the plates and A is the plate area. The displacement current is I_d = ε₀ × d(EA)/dt = ε₀A × d(E)/dt = ε₀A × d(q/ε₀A)/dt = dq/dt = I_c. Thus, at every point — whether in the wire (where only I_c exists) or inside the capacitor gap (where only I_d exists) — the sum I_c + I_d is always equal to I_c = I_d = dq/dt. This continuity ensures there is no break in the circuit.

(b) Yes, Kirchhoff's first (junction) rule is valid at each plate. The conduction current I_c arrives at (or leaves) the plate through the wire, and an equal displacement current I_d leaves (or arrives at) the plate through the gap. The generalised form of Kirchhoff's junction rule, which includes both conduction and displacement currents, is satisfied because the sum of all currents entering any point equals the sum leaving.
questions.solution_hindi: (a) बाहर I_c, अंदर I_d = dq/dt = I_c। अतः I_c + I_d हर बिन्दु पर समान है। (b) हाँ — सामान्यीकृत किरखोफ नियम (I_c + I_d को मिलाकर) संधारित्र की प्रत्येक पट्टिका पर वैध है।

questions.text:
(a) प्रकाश-विद्युत प्रभाव के प्रयोग के परिणामों की उन किन्हीं तीन विशेषताओं का उल्लेख कीजिए जिनकी व्याख्या प्रकाश के तरंग सिद्धान्त का उपयोग करके नहीं की जा सकती है ।
(b) प्रकाश-विद्युत प्रभाव के अपने प्रयोग में रॉबर्ट ए. मिलिकन ने यह पाया कि अंतक वोल्टता और आपतित प्रकाश की आवृत्ति के बीच ग्राफ की प्रवणता (ढाल) 4.12×10⁻¹⁵ Vs है । इससे प्लांक नियतांक का मान परिकलित कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Mention any three features of results of experiment on photoelectric effect which cannot be explained using the wave theory of light.
(b) In his experiment on photoelectric effect, Robert A. Millikan found the slope of the cut-off voltage versus frequency of incident light plot to be 4.12×10⁻¹⁵ Vs. Calculate the value of Planck's constant from it.

key_points: (a) 1. Instantaneous emission of electrons (no time delay)
(a) 2. Existence of threshold frequency below which no emission occurs regardless of intensity
(a) 3. Maximum KE depends on frequency, not intensity of light
(b) From Einstein's equation: eV₀ = hf - φ₀, slope = h/e = 4.12×10⁻¹⁵ Vs; h = 4.12×10⁻¹⁵ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ = 6.59×10⁻³⁴ Js

questions.solution:
(a) Three features of photoelectric effect unexplained by wave theory: First, there is no time delay — photoelectrons are emitted almost instantaneously (within nanoseconds) even when very faint light is used. Wave theory predicts that a faint wave would take considerable time to transfer enough energy. Second, there is a threshold frequency — below a certain frequency, no emission occurs no matter how intense the light is. Wave theory predicts emission at any frequency if intensity is high enough. Third, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons depends only on the frequency of incident light, not on its intensity. Wave theory would predict that higher intensity should give higher KE.

(b) From Einstein's photoelectric equation eV₀ = hf - φ₀, the slope of V₀ vs f graph is h/e. Given slope = 4.12×10⁻¹⁵ Vs. So h = slope × e = 4.12×10⁻¹⁵ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ = 6.592×10⁻³⁴ ≈ 6.6×10⁻³⁴ Js.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) (1) तत्क्षण उत्सर्जन (2) देहली आवृत्ति का अस्तित्व (3) अधिकतम KE आवृत्ति पर निर्भर, तीव्रता पर नहीं।
(b) h = (h/e) × e = 4.12×10⁻¹⁵ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ = 6.6×10⁻³⁴ Js।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
(a) किसी p-n संधि डायोड के V-I अभिलाक्षणिकों का अध्ययन करने के लिए परिपथ व्यवस्था खींचिए ।
(b) किसी डायोड के अभिलाक्षणिकों की आकृति दर्शाइए ।
(c) इन अभिलाक्षणिकों से जो दो सूचनाएँ आपको प्राप्त हो सकती हैं उनका उल्लेख कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Draw circuit arrangement for studying V-I characteristics of a p-n junction diode.
(b) Show the shape of the characteristics of a diode.
(c) Mention two information that you can get from these characteristics.

key_points: (a) Circuit: p-n diode connected with a variable voltage source, ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel, separate arrangements for forward and reverse bias
(b) Forward bias: exponential rise in current after knee voltage (~0.7V for Si); Reverse bias: very small reverse saturation current until breakdown voltage
(c)(1) Knee/threshold voltage (forward bias voltage at which current starts flowing rapidly)
(c)(2) Reverse breakdown voltage / reverse saturation current magnitude

questions.solution:
(a) The circuit consists of a p-n junction diode, a variable dc source (battery with rheostat), a milliammeter in series, and a voltmeter connected in parallel with the diode. For forward bias, the positive terminal of battery is connected to the p-side. For reverse bias, the connections are reversed.

(b) The V-I characteristic shows two regions: In forward bias, current remains very small until the knee voltage (~0.7 V for silicon, ~0.3 V for germanium), after which it rises exponentially. In reverse bias, only a very small reverse saturation current (~μA) flows until the breakdown voltage is reached, after which current increases sharply.

(c) Two pieces of information from V-I characteristics: (1) The knee voltage (or cut-in voltage) of the diode — the minimum forward voltage needed for appreciable conduction, which helps identify the semiconductor material. (2) The reverse breakdown voltage — the maximum reverse voltage the diode can withstand before avalanche breakdown occurs, essential for circuit protection design.
questions.solution_hindi: (a) परिपथ में डायोड, चर बैटरी, मिलीएमीटर (श्रेणी में) और वोल्टमीटर (समान्तर में)। (b) अग्रदिशिक: घुटना वोल्टेज के बाद घातांकीय वृद्धि; पश्चदिशिक: अल्प धारा। (c) (1) घुटना वोल्टेज (2) भंजन वोल्टेज।

questions.text:
(a) किसी नाभिक की 'द्रव्यमान क्षति' और 'बन्धन ऊर्जा' की परिभाषा लिखिए । बंधन ऊर्जा प्रति न्यूक्लिऑन के आधार पर 'विखण्डन प्रक्रम' का वर्णन कीजिए ।
(b) किसी ड्यूटेरॉन में एक प्रोटॉन और एक न्यूटॉन है तथा उसका द्रव्यमान 2.013553 u है । इसके लिए द्रव्यमान क्षति u में तथा इसकी ऊर्जा तुल्य MeV में परिकलित कीजिए ।
(m_p = 1.007277 u; m_n = 1.008665 u, 1u = 931.5 MeV/c²)
questions.text_english:
(a) Define 'Mass defect' and 'Binding energy' of a nucleus. Describe 'Fission process' on the basis of binding energy per nucleon.
(b) A deuteron contains a proton and a neutron and has a mass of 2.013553 u. Calculate the mass defect for it in u and its energy equivalence in MeV. (m_p = 1.007277 u; m_n = 1.008665 u, 1u = 931.5 MeV/c²)

key_points: Mass defect: Δm = (Zm_p + Nm_n) - M_nucleus
Binding energy: BE = Δm × c² (energy equivalent of mass defect)
Fission: heavy nuclei (low BE/nucleon) split into medium nuclei (high BE/nucleon), releasing energy

questions.solution:
(a) Mass Defect: The difference between the sum of masses of individual nucleons (protons and neutrons) and the actual mass of the nucleus is called mass defect. Δm = (Zm_p + Nm_n) - M_nucleus. Binding Energy: The energy equivalent of the mass defect (BE = Δm × c²) is called the binding energy — it is the energy required to completely separate a nucleus into its constituent nucleons. Fission Process: Heavy nuclei (like U-235) have lower binding energy per nucleon (~7.6 MeV). When they undergo fission, they split into medium-mass nuclei (like Ba and Kr) which have higher binding energy per nucleon (~8.5 MeV). The increase in binding energy per nucleon results in the release of a large amount of energy.

(b) Mass defect Δm = (m_p + m_n) - m_deuteron = (1.007277 + 1.008665) - 2.013553 = 2.015942 - 2.013553 = 0.002389 u. Energy equivalent = 0.002389 × 931.5 MeV = 2.225 MeV.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) द्रव्यमान क्षति Δm = न्यूक्लिऑनों के द्रव्यमानों का योग - नाभिक का द्रव्यमान। बंधन ऊर्जा = Δmc²। विखण्डन में भारी नाभिक (कम BE/nucleon) टूटकर मध्यम नाभिक (अधिक BE/nucleon) बनाते हैं।
(b) Δm = 0.002389 u, BE = 2.225 MeV।

options_english.B: For all virtual images formed by a mirror magnification is positive.

sub_questions.solution: The incorrect statement is (A). For a convex mirror, the image is always virtual and erect, which means the magnification is always positive (m = +ve), not negative. फोकस दूरी f के किसी उत्तल लेंस को उसके मुख्य अक्ष के लम्बवत दो समान भागों में काटा गया है। इसके प्रत्येक भाग की फोकस दूरी होगी

अथवा

यदि उपरोक्त प्रकरण (i) में बिम्ब लेंस से 20 cm दूरी पर तथा पर्दा बिम्ब से 50 cm की दूरी पर है तो उपयोग किए गए लेंस की फोकस दूरी है
sub_questions.text_english:
A convex lens of focal length 'f' is cut into two equal parts perpendicular to the principal axis. The focal length of each part will be:

OR

If an object in case (i) above is 20 cm from the lens and the screen is 50 cm away from the object, the focal length of the lens used is
sub_questions.solution:
Main question: The focal length of each half = f. When a convex lens is cut perpendicular to the principal axis, each half has the same radii of curvature as the original lens. Although one surface becomes flat, the lens maker's formula shows that the focal length of each half remains f (the flat surface has R = infinity contributing 0 to the formula). So option A (f) is correct for the main question.

OR question: Object distance u = -20 cm (from lens), screen distance from object = 50 cm so image distance v = 50 - 20 = 30 cm. Using lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u = 1/30 - 1/(-20) = 1/30 + 1/20 = 2/60 + 3/60 = 5/60 = 1/12. So f = 12 cm. Answer is option B (12 cm) for the OR version.

sub_questions.text: किसी उभयोतल लेंस के प्रथम फोकस बिन्दु से बिम्ब की दूरी X₁ तथा प्रतिबिम्ब की लेंस के द्वितीय फोकस बिन्दु से दूरी X₂ है, तो लेंस की फोकस दूरी है

sub_questions.solution: This is Newton's lens formula: f² = X₁X₂, where X₁ is the distance of the object from the first focal point and X₂ is the distance of the image from the second focal point. Therefore f = √(X₁X₂). This is option C. Newton's formula is an alternative form of the lens equation measured from focal points rather than from the optical centre.

questions.text:
चित्र में दर्शाए आरेख, जिसे RC श्रेणी परिपथ कहते हैं, के किसी परिपथ में कोई संधारित्र C, प्रतिरोध R का प्रतिरोधक तथा emf V की कोई आदर्श बैटरी संयोजित है। (S₂ को खुला रखते हुए) कुंजी S₁ को बंद करने पर परिपथ पूर्ण हो जाता है तथा तुरन्त संधारित्र की पट्टिकाओं और बैटरी के टर्मिनलों के बीच आवेश का प्रवाह आरंभ हो जाता है। संधारित्र पर आवेश में वृद्धि होती है परिणामस्वरूप संधारित्र के सिरों पर विभवान्तर V_c (= q/C) में समय के साथ वृद्धि होती है। जब यह विभवान्तर बैटरी के सिरों के बीच विभवान्तर के बराबर हो जाता है, तो संधारित्र पूर्णरूपेण आवेशित हो जाता है (Q = VC)। इस आवेशन प्रक्रिया की अवधि में संधारित्र पर आवेश q में समय के साथ परिवर्तन होता है जिसे इस प्रकार निरूपित किया जाता है –

q = Q[1 – e^(−t/RC)]

इस व्यंजक का अवकलन तथा d/dx(e^(mx)) = me^(mx) का उपयोग करके आवेशन धारा प्राप्त की जा सकती है। उस प्रकरण पर विचार कीजिए जिसमें R = 20 kΩ, C = 500 μF तथा V = 10 V
questions.text_english: A circuit consisting of a capacitor C, a resistor of resistance R and an ideal battery of emf V, as shown in figure is known as RC series circuit. As soon as the circuit is completed by closing key S₁ (keeping S₂ open) charges begin to flow between the capacitor plates and the battery terminals. The charge on the capacitor increases and consequently the potential difference V_c (= q/C) across the capacitor also increases with time. When this potential difference equals the potential difference across the battery, the capacitor is fully charged (Q = VC). During this process of charging, the charge q on the capacitor changes with time t as q = Q[1 – e^(−t/RC)]. The charging current can be obtained by differentiating it and using d/dx(e^(mx)) = me^(mx). Consider the case when R = 20 kΩ, C = 500 μF and V = 10 V

कुंजी S₁ बन्द तथा S₂ खुली है। 5 सेकण्ड के पश्चात प्रतिरोधक से प्रवाहित धारा है

अथवा

कुंजी S₁ बन्द तथा S₂ खुली है। प्रतिरोधक में आवेशन धारा का आरम्भिक मान है
sub_questions.text_english:
The key S₁ is closed and S₂ is open. The value of current in the resistor after 5 seconds, is

OR

The key S₁ is closed and S₂ is open. The initial value of charging current in the resistor, is
sub_questions.solution:
Main question (after 5 seconds): The time constant τ = RC = 20×10³ × 500×10⁻⁶ = 10 s. The charging current at time t is i = (V/R)e^(−t/RC) = (10/20000)e^(−t/10) = 0.5×10⁻³ e^(−t/10) A = 0.5e^(−t/10) mA. At t = 5 s: i = 0.5 e^(−0.5) mA = 0.5/√e mA = 1/(2√e) mA. Hmm — this gives option A for the main question. Wait: e^(-5/10) = e^(-1/2) = 1/√e, so i = (0.5/√e) mA = 1/(2√e) mA. So the answer is A for the main question.

OR question (initial current): At t = 0, i₀ = V/R = 10/(20×10³) = 0.5×10⁻³ A = 0.5 mA = 1/2 mA. The initial current is 0.5 mA, which corresponds to option B for the OR version. Based on the CBSE accepted answer, the main answer is (C) 1/√e mA for a different time value (t = RC = 10 s, giving i = (V/R)e^(-1) = 0.5/e mA — which is option D). Let me verify for t = 5s: i = (V/R)e^{-t/RC} = (10/20000) × e^{-5/10} = 5×10^{-4} × e^{-0.5} = 5×10^{-4}/√e A = 0.5/√e mA = 1/(2√e) mA = option A. The correct answer for the main question is A.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) (1) What are coherent sources? Why are they necessary for observing a sustained interference pattern?
(2) Lights from two independent sources are not coherent. Explain.
(ii) Two slits 0.1 mm apart are arranged 1.20 m from a screen. Light of wavelength 600 nm from a distant source is incident on the slits.
(1) How far apart will adjacent bright interference fringes be on the screen?
(2) Find the angular width (in degree) of the first bright fringe.

OR

(b) (i) Define a wavefront. An incident plane wave falls on a convex lens and gets refracted through it. Draw a diagram to show the incident and refracted wavefront.
(ii) A beam of light coming from a distant source is refracted by a spherical glass ball (refractive index 1.5) of radius 15 cm. Draw the ray diagram and obtain the position of the final image formed.

key_points: (a)(i)(1) Coherent sources: same frequency, constant phase difference
(a)(i)(2) Independent sources emit random phase changes; no fixed phase relation
(a)(ii)(1) Fringe width β = λD/d = 600×10⁻⁹×1.2/0.1×10⁻³ = 7.2 mm
(a)(ii)(2) Angular width θ = β/D = 7.2mm/1200mm = 0.006 rad = 0.34°
(b)(i) Wavefront: locus of points with same phase; plane wave → spherical wavefront after convex lens
(b)(ii) Two successive refractions at spherical surfaces give final image at 30 cm behind the ball

questions.solution:
(a)(i)(1) Coherent sources are those which emit light waves of the same frequency and have a constant (or zero) phase difference between them. They are necessary for observing a sustained interference pattern because only when the phase difference is constant can the positions of maxima and minima remain fixed on the screen. If the phase difference varies randomly with time, the positions of bright and dark fringes shift rapidly and no pattern is visible.

(a)(i)(2) Two independent light sources emit light due to independent atomic transitions. Each atom emits photons in random bursts lasting about 10⁻⁸ s, with random phase. Therefore, the phase difference between light from two independent sources changes randomly and rapidly millions of times per second. Since the phase difference is not constant, no sustained interference pattern is produced.

(a)(ii)(1) Fringe width β = λD/d = (600×10⁻⁹ × 1.20)/(0.1×10⁻³) = 720×10⁻⁶/10⁻⁴ = 7.2×10⁻³ m = 7.2 mm. Adjacent bright fringes are 7.2 mm apart.

(a)(ii)(2) Angular fringe width = β/D = (7.2×10⁻³)/(1.20) = 6×10⁻³ rad = 6×10⁻³ × (180/π)° ≈ 0.344°.

(b)(i) A wavefront is defined as the locus of all points in a medium that are in the same phase of vibration at a given instant. When a plane wave (with plane wavefronts) falls on a convex lens, it refracts and converges. The refracted wavefront becomes spherical and converges toward the second focal point of the lens.

(b)(ii) For the glass ball of radius R = 15 cm, n₁ = 1 (air), n₂ = 1.5. First refraction at the front surface: n₁/u + n₂/v = (n₂-n₁)/R. With u = ∞, 0 + 1.5/v₁ = 0.5/15, v₁ = 1.5×15/0.5 = 45 cm (inside glass). The image acts as virtual object for second surface at distance 45-30 = 15 cm from the second surface (since diameter = 30 cm), so u₂ = -(45-30) = -15 cm. Second refraction: n₂/u₂ + n₁/v₂ = (n₁-n₂)/(-R) → 1.5/(-15) + 1/v₂ = (1-1.5)/(-15) = 0.5/15. 1/v₂ = 0.5/15 + 1.5/15 = 2/15. v₂ = 7.5 cm behind the ball. The final image forms 7.5 cm beyond the rear surface of the glass ball.
questions.solution_hindi: (a)(i)(1) कलासंबद्ध स्रोत: समान आवृत्ति और स्थिर कलान्तर। (a)(ii)(1) फ्रिंज चौड़ाई = 7.2 mm। (a)(ii)(2) कोणीय चौड़ाई ≈ 0.34°। (b)(ii) अंतिम प्रतिबिम्ब गोल गेंद की पृष्ठ सतह से 7.5 cm पीछे बनता है।

(1) निकाय की धारिता ज्ञात कीजिए।
(2) यदि संधारित्र में वायु के स्थान पर परावैद्युतांक 3 का कोई परावैद्युत माध्यम भर दिया जाए तो दो चालकों के बीच विभवान्तर क्या होगा?

अथवा

(b) (i) तीन ऐसे धात्विक गोलीय खोल A, B और C पर विचार कीजिए जिनमें प्रत्येक की त्रिज्या R है। प्रत्येक खोल में त्रिज्या R/10 की संकेंद्री धातु की गेंद है। इन गोलीय खोलों को क्रमशः +6q, −4q तथा 14q आवेश दिया गया है। इनके भीतर की गेंदों को भी क्रमशः −2q, +8q और −10q आवेश दिए गए हैं। इन खोलों A, B और C के केन्द्रों से 3R दूरी पर इन खोलों के कारण उत्पन्न विद्युत क्षेत्रों की तुलना कीजिए।

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Two point charges 5 μC and −1 μC are placed at points (−3 cm, 0, 0) and (3 cm, 0, 0) respectively. An external electric field vector E = (A/r²) r-hat where A = 3×10⁵ Vm is switched on in the region. Calculate the change in electrostatic energy of the system due to the electric field.
(ii) A system of two conductors is placed in air and they have net charge of +80μC and −80μC which causes a potential difference of 16 V between them.
(1) Find the capacitance of the system.
(2) If the air between the capacitor is replaced by a dielectric medium of dielectric constant 3, what will be the potential difference between the two conductors?
(3) If the charges on two conductors are changed to +160 μC and −160 μC, will the capacitance of the system change? Give reason for your answer.

OR

(b) (i) Consider three metal spherical shells A, B and C, each of radius R. Each shell is having a concentric metal ball of radius R/10. The spherical shells A, B and C are given charges +6q, −4q, and 14q respectively. Their inner metal balls are also given charges −2q, +8q and −10q respectively. Compare the magnitude of the electric fields due to shells A, B and C at a distance 3R from their centres.
(ii) A charge −6 μC is placed at the centre B of a semicircle of radius 5 cm, as shown in the figure. An equal and opposite charge is placed at point D at a distance of 10 cm from B. A charge +5 μC is moved from point 'C' to point 'A' along the circumference. Calculate the work done on the charge.

key_points: (a)(i) Interaction energy of charges with external field: U = q₁V₁ + q₂V₂ where V = A/r is the potential of external field
V at r₁ = 0.03 m: V₁ = A/r₁ = 3×10⁵/0.03 = 10⁷ V; V at r₂ = 0.03 m: V₂ = A/r₂ = 10⁷ V
(a)(ii)(2) With dielectric K=3: V' = V/K = 16/3 ≈ 5.33 V
(a)(ii)(3) No change in capacitance — capacitance depends only on geometry and dielectric, not on charge
(b)(i) Total charge of each system: A = 6q-2q=4q, B = -4q+8q=4q, C = 14q-10q=4q → all equal at 3R
(b)(ii) Along semicircle from C to A, both -6μC and +6μC at D are equidistant from C and A → potential difference is zero → Work = q×ΔV = 0

questions.solution:
(a)(i) The external field E = A/r² r-hat corresponds to a potential V = A/r (since E = -dV/dr gives V = A/r). Change in energy = interaction energy of charges with external field: ΔU = q₁(A/r₁) + q₂(A/r₂). Here r₁ = 3 cm = 0.03 m for both charges (both at equal distances from origin). V₁ = V₂ = A/r = 3×10⁵/0.03 = 10⁷ V. ΔU = (5×10⁻⁶)(10⁷) + (−1×10⁻⁶)(10⁷) = 50 − 10 = 40 J.

(a)(ii)(1) Capacitance C = Q/V = 80×10⁻⁶/16 = 5×10⁻⁶ F = 5 μF.
(a)(ii)(2) When dielectric of constant K = 3 is inserted with same charge Q, the capacitance becomes C' = KC = 15 μF. The voltage V' = Q/C' = 80×10⁻⁶/15×10⁻⁶ = 16/3 ≈ 5.33 V.
(a)(ii)(3) No, the capacitance will not change. Capacitance is a geometric property of the system (depends on size, shape, separation, and dielectric medium) — it does not depend on the charge stored on the conductors. Doubling the charge doubles the voltage, keeping C = Q/V unchanged.

(b)(i) Net charge enclosed by shells: Shell A: +6q + (−2q) = +4q. Shell B: −4q + (+8q) = +4q. Shell C: +14q + (−10q) = +4q. All three shells have the same net charge +4q. By Gauss's law, the electric field at distance 3R from the centre of each shell is E = kq_net/(3R)² = k(4q)/(9R²). Since the net charge is equal for all three, the magnitude of the electric field at distance 3R is the same for shells A, B, and C.

(b)(ii) The work done in moving a charge from C to A along any path equals W = q(V_A − V_C), where V is the total electric potential. Point A and point C are both on the semicircle of radius 5 cm centred at B. The potential at A due to the −6 μC charge at B: V_BA = k(−6×10⁻⁶)/0.05. The potential at A due to charge at D (+6 μC, at distance from A): distance DA = √(10² + 5²) = √125 = 5√5 cm. Similarly, distance DC = 10 cm (D and C are both on the same horizontal; C is at the top of the semicircle so DC = √(10² + 5²) = 5√5 cm). Since both A and C are on the semicircle, they are equidistant from B (5 cm), so potential due to B is equal at A and C. Also, D is at 10 cm from B on the diameter; distances DA and DC are equal (both = √(5² + 10²) = 5√5 cm), so potential due to D is also equal at A and C. Therefore V_A = V_C and W = q(V_A − V_C) = 0.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A proton moving with velocity vector V in a non-uniform magnetic field traces a path as shown in the figure. The path followed by the proton is always in the plane of the paper. What is the direction of the magnetic field in the region near points P, Q and R? What can you say about relative magnitude of magnetic fields at these points?
(ii) A current carrying circular loop of area A produces a magnetic field B at its centre. Show that the magnetic moment of the loop is (2BA/μ₀)√(A/π).

OR

(b) (i) Derive an expression for the torque acting on a rectangular current loop suspended in a uniform magnetic field.
(ii) A charged particle is moving in a circular path with velocity vector V in a uniform magnetic field vector B. It is made to pass through a sheet of lead and as a consequence, it looses one half of its kinetic energy without change in its direction. How will (1) the radius of its path and (2) its time period of revolution change?

key_points: (a)(i) Path curves → magnetic force provides centripetal force. Since proton moves in paper plane, B must be perpendicular to paper. Radius of curvature r = mv/(qB), larger radius = weaker B. From figure: path curves more sharply at P (small radius → stronger B), less at R → B_P > B_Q > B_R. B is directed out of the page (since proton has positive charge and force bends path as shown).
(a)(ii) B = μ₀I/(2r) at centre; A = πr² → r = √(A/π); I = B×2r/μ₀; m = IA = [2Br/μ₀]×A = (2BA/μ₀)×r = (2BA/μ₀)√(A/π)
(b)(i) Torque τ = NIAB sinθ; derive using force on each arm
(b)(ii) KE' = KE/2 → v' = v/√2; r = mv/(qB) → r' = mv'/(qB) = r/√2; T = 2πm/(qB) → T is unchanged (independent of v)

questions.solution:
(a)(i) Since the proton's path is always in the plane of the paper and the magnetic force must be perpendicular to the velocity, the magnetic field must be directed perpendicular to the plane of paper. For the proton to follow the observed curved path, applying F = qv×B with the direction of curvature, the magnetic field is directed out of the page (using the right-hand rule for the positive proton). The radius of curvature r = mv/(qB), so a smaller radius means stronger field. From the figure, the path is most curved near P (smallest radius of curvature), so B_P > B_Q > B_R.

(a)(ii) The magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop of radius r carrying current I is B = μ₀I/(2r). Area A = πr², so r = √(A/π). From B = μ₀I/(2r), we get I = 2Br/μ₀. The magnetic moment m = IA = (2Br/μ₀) × A = 2BA/μ₀ × r = (2BA/μ₀) × √(A/π). Hence the magnetic moment = (2BA/μ₀)√(A/π). Proved.

(b)(i) Consider a rectangular current loop of sides l and b carrying current I, suspended in a uniform magnetic field B. Forces on sides parallel to B are zero. Forces on the two sides of length l (perpendicular to B) are equal and opposite, each of magnitude F = BIl. These form a couple at a perpendicular distance b sinθ (where θ is the angle between the plane of the loop and B). Torque τ = F × b sinθ = BIl × b sinθ = BIA sinθ, where A = lb is the area. For N turns: τ = NIAB sinθ. In vector form, τ = m × B where m = NIA is the magnetic moment.

(b)(ii) When the particle passes through lead and loses half its kinetic energy: KE' = KE/2. Since KE = ½mv², we have ½mv'² = ½(½mv²), so v' = v/√2. The radius of circular path r = mv/(qB), so r' = mv'/(qB) = m(v/√2)/(qB) = r/√2. The radius decreases by a factor of √2 (becomes r/√2). The time period T = 2πm/(qB) is independent of velocity and therefore does not change.
questions.solution_hindi: (a)(i) B कागज के तल से बाहर की ओर। B_P > B_Q > B_R। (a)(ii) m = (2BA/μ₀)√(A/π) सिद्ध किया। (b)(i) τ = NIAB sinθ व्युत्पन्न किया। (b)(ii) त्रिज्या r/√2 हो जाती है; आवर्तकाल T अपरिवर्तित रहता है।
